subject: Post-call: Vector sizing, auth & routing follow-up for RetailCo POC
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ramirez <sofia@retailco.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Post-call: Vector sizing, auth & routing follow-up for RetailCo POC

Hi Sofia — great call this morning, thanks for walking us through the search/rerank workflow and the current constraints. Quick written recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned before Ben/Monica loop in on the architecture details.

Recap (what you told us)
- Primary use case: semantic search -> reranker for product discovery on web/mobile.
- Current vectors: 1536 dim from ProviderX; batch size ~64, store in a managed vector DB.
- Hard constraints: 100ms p90 latency for retrieval+rerank for web reads; peak ingest bursts ~1.2M vectors/day during catalog updates.
- SSO: SAML-based IdP + need for cross-account service account for background ingest jobs.

Questions we raised on call (answered live):
- Open to model variants with 1024 dims if unit cost/latency improves and quality delta is acceptable.
- Prefer to keep a single canonical vector space during migration to preserve existing feature pipeline.

Proposal / next steps from Redwood (high level)
1) Proof-of-concept (2 weeks): run a Redwood-hosted retrieval+rerank pipeline against a 100k sample (we’ll test 1536 vs 1024 and quantized variants).
2) Auth & routing: demo service-account based auth for ingest + per-route routing to Dedicated pool for low-latency reads. We’ll provide an SSO checklist for your IdP.
3) Migration plan: produce a canonical re-index path + backfill plan to avoid double-serving during cutover.
4) Measurement: we’ll return precision@10, end-to-end 95/99 latency, and cost per 1k queries for each candidate vector size and quantization profile.

Deliverables we’ll send by EOD Monday: short design doc (vector sizing tradeoffs), suggested batching defaults for RetailCo workload, and the SSO checklist.

Can you confirm the sample dataset (the CSV you mentioned) is okay to share with us for the POC? If there are any export controls or fields to strip, please call that out.

Thanks — I’ll attach the proposal and Ben/Monica will follow with architecture notes.

—
Rachel Kim
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.ai
From: Sofia Ramirez <sofia@retailco.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: RetailCo API <api-team@retailco.com>, RetailCo DevOps <devops@retailco.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Feb 2026 11:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-call: Vector sizing, auth & routing follow-up for RetailCo POC

Thanks Rachel — that matches our notes. Confirming:
- We will share a 100k-sample CSV (product title, description, sku, current_vector) — stripping PII is done already.
- We’re currently on ProviderX vectors (1536) and would prefer not to degrade relevance; open to 1024 if you can show parity on our eval set.
- Latency: 100ms p90 is a hard target for web; mobile can tolerate up to 150ms p90.
- Auth: we have a SAML IdP; DevOps will need a service account key or role for the ingest pipeline.

One note on storage: our infra team prefers to keep vectors in our cloud account. Is Redwood able to serve retrieval from a customer-owned VPC/Private deployment and still provide the same routing/fallback logic?

Sofia
Sofia Ramirez
Head of Search
RetailCo
sofia@retailco.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 09:18:00 -0500
Subject: RE: Post-call: Vector sizing, auth & routing follow-up for RetailCo POC

Quick internal notes after reading the RetailCo replies — agenda for our architecture email back to them:
1) Vector size experiments: run three arms on the sample set
- A: 1536 (baseline, ProviderX embeddings)
- B: 1024 dense Redwood embedding (float16)
- C: 1024 quantized (4-bit) variant for cost/latency tradeoffs
2) Normalization: compare L2-normalized vectors (cosine sims) vs raw dot-product after length-scaling; our initial bias is to normalize for cross-vendor parity.
3) Batching & ingest: propose adaptive batching with max_batch=256 for bulk backfills and target_batch=32 for steady-state streaming to keep latency predictable.
4) Storage/routing: customer-owned VPC option is supported — Redwood Private can co-locate vector store in RetailCo VPC and expose per-route signed tokens. Fallback routing: prefer Dedicated in us-east-1, fallback to hosted read-only pool if Dedicated capacity saturated.
5) Auth: provide short-lived service tokens (OIDC) for ingest jobs + SAML SSO for console access. We’ll include a minimal IAM policy template.

Action items for us (Ben/Monica/Karthik):
- Draft the vector sizing proposal + sample-run plan (Ben)
- Prepare SSO/service-account checklist & IAM policy (Monica)
- Validate Private deployment routing docs + latency SLOs (Karthik)

I’ll attach a small sketch of batching behavior and expected per-token costs for the three arms.

—Ben
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ramirez <sofia@retailco.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 14:40:00 -0500
Subject: Proposed POC plan + files (attached) — RetailCo vector sizing

Sofia — attaching the 1-page proposal and the SSO checklist (see attachments). High-level POC steps:

POC (2 weeks) — what we’ll run
- Day 0–1: ingest sample 100k into a sandbox (we’ll use your VPC option if you prefer; attach SSO checklist)
- Day 2–7: run three experimental arms (1536 baseline / 1024 float16 / 1024 4-bit) — measure precision@10 and end-to-end 95/99 latency
- Day 8–10: fine-tune batching and caching knobs (adaptive batching + KV prefix cache)
- Day 11–14: finalize recommendations and migration cutover playbook

Data handling: Redwood will provide a short pipeline (S3 -> Redwood ingest) with a service account role limited to PutObject + ListBucket. For the private deployment option, vectors stay in your cloud account and our control plane coordinates routing; we only ask for a signed-service-account token for reads.

Please confirm these three things so we can schedule the sandbox and allocate Dedicated pool capacity for the web-read SLO:
- Confirm we can receive the 100k sample CSV by Monday noon ET.
- Confirm RetailCo prefers the Private/VPC option or Redwood-hosted sandbox.
- Any internal compliance note (e.g., fields to redact) we should be aware of.

Attachments:
- 20260215-vector-sizing-proposal.pdf (1 page)
- sso-setup-checklist.md

If this looks good I’ll schedule a kickoff with Ben and Karthik for Tuesday.

Cheers,
Rachel

DevOps will confirm the exact role ARN and the SAML metadata endpoint by EOD Monday.

—RetailCo DevOps
